page.layout: One title page, centred. Top: printed author name in capitals with a line of small caps below, then the large title in red and black, followed by the subtitle, the red "CORONAE VI." line, and six lines of contents (I–VI) with italic text. Below these: red line of dedication, then a red imprint line of two lines. Centre: woodcut medallion with initials "I. L." left and "P. R." right, then the red imprint "Herbornae Nassoviorum, 1651." at the foot.

main_text.l: I. De regnorum dignitate, adquisitione, conservatione, vigore, fatalibus limitibus & periodis, ruinâ denique & interitu.
II. De Regum & Principum dignitate atque officio, eorundemq; in tyrannos degenerantium interitu.
III. De Regum & Principum Consiliariis, Legatis, Officiariis, cæterisq; aulicis.
V. De Conjugibus, Parentibus, Liberis, Fratribus & Cognatis.
VI. De bellis, bellorumq; ducibus & auxiliis, de hostibus item, victoriâ, & pace.
Recensente Cyriaco Lentulo, Politices & antiquitatum latinarum & gracarum Herborna Professore.

page.notes: The printed "posthumum" appears with a superscript mark/abbreviation over the "m" (rendered as "posthumum" with a tilde-like stroke); the stroke is read as a macron-type abbreviation and transcribed as printed. Dedication word "incremento" and "Professore" are as printed; "Opus incremento posthumum" is the printed red line. The woodcut medallion shows a seated figure in a landscape; the handwritten "P" mark at the upper right is handwriting and omitted. Ornamental top-left letterforms and faint show-through from the reverse are omitted. Left edge is cut; the initial "F" of "FLORUM" is partly cut off by the scan edge and the roman numeral "I." of item I is partially cut. Some small italic words in the contents list are uncertain: "conservatione," and "Consiliariis" were read with reasonable confidence. The printed "Herbornæ Nassoviorum, 1651" line is red and has no further text.
